clue.text: Policeman mistaken to avoid commitment

parts.note: cop is slang for a police officer
out means wrong, as in a reckoning that is out by ten

explanation.surface: An officer who got it wrong tries to dodge any obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: To back out of a promise or duty is the phrasal verb in question, an evasion of an obligation.

clue.text: Tackle study with assurance

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
front means brazen nerve or effrontery

explanation.surface: Someone approaches a problem by studying it with confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a problem is to face up to it squarely.

clue.text: Rap spots arranged for them?

indicators.note: arranged signals that the letters of the two words are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A rap gig's time slots have been booked for some celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges RAP SPOTS; the whole clue also describes the answer, since performers have gig slots booked for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Chart musicians are the people for whom performance slots are booked.

clue.text: Drug addict taking heroin from court official

indicators.note: taking ... from signals that one letter is removed from the official's title

parts.note: an usher keeps order in a courtroom
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: An addict steals heroin from a court official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' with 'from' removes H from USHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes drugs habitually is called a user.

clue.text: Concerned with teaching reformed addict I caught

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters of the word addict are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A former addict, now a teacher, talks about being caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' rearranges ADDICT into DIDACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactic writing or speech is intended to instruct.

clue.text: Unlikely to become reformed criminal,I rob nice girl

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of the following words are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A hardened criminal confesses to robbing a pleasant girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges I ROB NICE GIRL; the page shows the I as a figure 1.
explanation.definitionFit: An incorrigible person is beyond correction, a habitual offender who cannot be improved.

clue.text: Reckon on having to do this in class

definitions.text: Reckon on having to do this in class

parts.words: Reckon on having to do this in class
parts.note: pupils expecting to do sums in a school lesson: to reckon is to calculate, and this subject is one of the three Rs

explanation.surface: Someone expects to face this task at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reckon on' reads as 'expect', but 'reckon' is also to calculate, which is what pupils do in this lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: The school subject of sums and calculation is where children learn to reckon figures.

clue.text: Name of Roman earth goddess we demand to know

parts.note: ... as a command, means let me know
us is the object form of we

explanation.surface: Someone insists on hearing the name of the Roman goddess of the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'tell us!' is what people say when they demand to know something.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romans worshipped the earth mother as Tellus, also called Terra.

clue.text: Look after group on Greek island

indicators.note: on signals that the group comes next to the island in the answer

parts.note: Cos (or Kos) is an island in the Dodecanese
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: Someone takes care of a party staying on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts SET beside COS.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset someone is to pamper and care for them.

clue.text: Small drink for each kid

parts.note: a nip is a small measure of spirits
per means for each, as in two per person

explanation.surface: A small drink for every child at the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Nipper is informal British for a small child.

clue.text: Warrior indisposed, beset by pains

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the pains go around the word for indisposed

parts.note: aches are pains
ill means indisposed

explanation.surface: A soldier off sick is troubled by aches and pains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beset by' means surrounded by. The picture of a sick warrior suits the Greek hero, who died of a wound to the heel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero of the Trojan War was the greatest fighter at Troy.

clue.text: Chance romantic encounter making yogis tremble excitedly

indicators.note: excitedly suggests agitation, so the letters of yogis and tremble are stirred up

explanation.surface: A romantic meeting so thrilling it sets meditating yogis shaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' rearranges YOGIS TREMBLE; 'tremble' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock plot phrase for two strangers meeting and falling in love describes a chance romance.

clue.text: Curses vermin

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of annoyance, like drat

explanation.definitionFit: Rats! is an exclamation of irritation, and rats are rodent pests.

clue.text: You may be included in procedure where trial takes place

indicators.note: included in means placed inside, so the old word for you goes inside the procedure

parts.note: a course of action is a procedure
thou is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A defendant may be part of the process where a case is heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be included in' is the container signal; 'You' comes in its old form, thou, still heard in some dialects and in prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Trials are held in a court building.

clue.text: Writer producing French poster?

parts.note: Norman means from Normandy in France
a mailer is one who posts letters

explanation.surface: An author designs a poster in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poster' reads as a placard, but it is one who posts things. Norman Mailer was an American novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of The Naked and the Dead was a prominent American novelist.

clue.text: Musical film producing a stir in class

indicators.note: in signals that the stirring words go inside the abbreviation for class

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class
to rouse is to stir up

explanation.surface: A film musical causes a commotion in a school class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. Carousel is the Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical, filmed in 1956.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1956 Rodgers and Hammerstein screen adaptation is a celebrated musical movie.

clue.text: Really scoff about dealer you might get a ring from

definitions.text: dealer you might get a ring from

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for scoff wraps around the word for really

parts.note: to jeer is to scoff
well, as in 'well, I never', can mean really

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a trader who might phone them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. 'ring' suggests a phone call, but it is a piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader in gems and precious metals sells finger rings.

clue.text: I'll say it — one colleague's a bastard

parts.note: I'll gives its letters without the apostrophe
e.g. is short for for example, which say means
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
a mate is a colleague; the 's stands for is and gives nothing

explanation.surface: Someone is about to call a co-worker a rude name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is EG (for example), and the 's of 'colleague's' is 'is', linking to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bastard used as an adjective means born out of wedlock.

clue.text: Put an end to old tax on church

parts.note: scot was an old tax, as in scot-free

explanation.surface: Someone abolishes an ancient levy on the church.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOT survives in 'scot-free', meaning without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour or plan is to stop it.

clue.text: Ink, say, in brown container

indicators.note: in signals that the sound of the word ink goes inside the colour

parts.note: tan is a light brown

indicators.note: say signals a word as heard, so ink is spelt the way the abbreviation of incorporated is

parts.note: the word ink, spoken, gives the sound of the abbreviation for incorporated

explanation.surface: Ink is kept in a brown pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a soundalike: the company abbreviation Inc is pronounced like the writing fluid; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal food can is a receptacle for preserved goods.

clue.text: Stupidly, cold food is put inside

indicators.note: put inside signals that the food goes within the word for cold

parts.note: chilly means cold
a dish is a serving of food

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly puts cold food inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupidly' sits at the front like an anagram signal, but it is the definition; 'put inside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting like a child means acting in a silly, immature way.

clue.text: Drop off number less than twelve

indicators.note: less than means taken away from, so the number letter is removed from the word for twelve

parts.note: a dozen is twelve
N is the mathematical symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: A figure drops below twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than' looks like a comparison but removes N from DOZEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod off is to fall into a light sleep.

clue.text: International traveller detained by Interpol once

indicators.note: detained by means held inside, so the letters are concealed within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A globetrotter was once held by the international police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detained by' hides the answer in interPOL Once. Marco Polo was the Venetian traveller to China.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco the Venetian merchant journeyed across Asia to the court of Kublai Khan.

clue.text: Comfortably settled for the night, began eating

definitions.meaning: snug in bed with the covers pressed round
started on a meal with gusto

explanation.definitionFit: A child put to bed with the blankets tucked round them, and to tuck in is to start eating heartily.

clue.text: Well-known Jaguar owner's given learner a bit of a mouthful

parts.note: Inspector Morse, the TV detective, drove a Jaguar; the 's means has
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A famous car owner hands a learner driver something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse, of the British TV series set in Oxford, drove a red Jaguar car.
explanation.definitionFit: A small piece of food is a single bite.

clue.text: Really, is that how law abiding folk behave?-

definitions.meaning: the manner of people who keep the rules

explanation.definitionFit: Honestly! expresses disbelief, and decent folk act with integrity.

clue.text: Cricketer's hat

definitions.meaning: a player who delivers the ball
a hard round felt hat, the derby

explanation.definitionFit: The cricketer who delivers the ball, and the hard felt hat also called a derby.
